landed.summary: I re-read all six pages with qc.py. All six proposed values hold up and none is refuted. On NC State, 'Height: 15 ft. 0 in. - 33 ft. 0 in.' converts to 180-396 in and 'Width: 15 ft. 0 in. - 25 ft. 0 in.' converts to 180-300 in. The feet were converted, each min is at or below its max, the ranges come from the species page and not a cultivar, and the plant is not a climber. Both quotes appear verbatim as single lines, and both citation labels contain the literal field names. is_edible and attracts_pollinators are correctly null: every page I could fetch was silent on both. The unknowns contain one factual error. The researcher says ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/FP370 gave ProxyError on every attempt, but it fetched fine for me. It is the 'Lennei' cultivar page (Height 20 to 25 feet, Spread 15 to 25 feet) and says nothing about edibility or pollinators, so it would not have changed any value. That unknowns entry should say it was excluded as a cultivar page rather than that it was unreachable. MOBOT (a885) and Clemson did return ProxyError for me, which matches the researcher's notes.

unknowns: Toxicity (required accompaniment to is_edible=true): NC State Plant Toolbox lists this plant with medium poison severity to humans. Poison Part: Flowers, Fruits, Leaves, Seeds. Poison Symptoms: "The leaves, flowers, green fruits, ripe fruits and seeds contain cyanide compounds in detectable quantities, but the seeds and fruit stalks have the highest concentration of toxins. If a couple of pits (stones, which enclose the seeds) are accidentally swallowed, it will not cause poisoning, but care should be taken to remove pits before fruits are processed in a blender or any other machine that will crack open the pits. Symptoms include gasping, weakness, excitement, pupil dilation, spasms, convulsions, coma and respiratory failure." Poison Toxic Principle: Cyanogenic glycosides (amygdalin & prunasin). The page's tags also flag it as a problem for cats, dogs, and horses. Only the ripe fruit flesh is the edible part; the pits/seeds, leaves, and flowers are the toxic parts and must not be eaten.

RHS (rhs.org.uk/plants/13950/prunus-avium/details) gives size as open-ended 'Max Height Higher than 12 metres' and 'Max Spread wider than 8 metres' -- per instructions, an open-ended RHS bound gives no usable figure, so it was not used; NC State's concrete '15 to 30 feet with a matching spread' was used instead for both height and spread.

RHS 'grow-your-own' cherries page (rhs.org.uk/fruit/cherries/grow-your-own) was not used as a citation source because its size/edibility figures there are given for named cultivars and rootstocks, not the species Prunus avium itself (rule 3).

UGA confirms sweet cherry (Prunus avium) is grown for fruit and that sweet cherries other than 'Stella' are self-infertile and need cross-pollination; PSU gives only frost critical temperatures. Neither gives a cherry size figure or a toxicity statement, so neither changes a field.
Prunus avium is a tree, not a climber, so the size-nulling climber rule (rule 4) does not apply here.

landed.summary:
I re-read all the pages I could reach with qc.py: NC State, RHS 13950, RHS grow-your-own, UGA B992 and PSU. The MOBOT (plantfinder.mobot.org) fetch was blocked by the sandbox network proxy, as the task expected, and the record claims nothing from it.

All six proposed fields hold up. The size fields are 15 to 30 ft from NC State, which gives 180 to 360 in with the feet correctly converted. The range is published, min <= max, the page is species-level, and the plant is a tree, not a climber. Spread comes from NC State's 'with a matching spread', which is verified text. is_edible is supported by NC State ('Fruit edible raw or cooked.') and by the RHS 'Fruit Edible' tag. NC State's full cyanide/poison warning (medium severity) is carried verbatim in unknowns, so F passes. attracts_pollinators rests on the RHS 'Plants for pollinators' tag, and NC State corroborates it with its pollinator-garden prose and tag. All four quotes are verbatim single runs, and every citation label contains its field name.

One issue is not a refutation but a reviewer should look at it. RHS 13950 gives 'Max Height Higher than 12 metres' (more than 472 in) against NC State's 30 ft (360 in) maximum. The RHS figure is open-ended, so the run's rule excludes it, but the two sources do conflict on the upper end. Excluding the grow-your-own page was right: its sizes are all rootstock sizes ('Gisela 5' 3–4m, 'Colt' 6–8m), not species sizes. Minor wording problem in unknowns: it says UGA and PSU were 'not queried' and also that nothing was 'located' on them. That is self-contradictory. In fact UGA only confirms cherries are grown for fruit and have cross-pollination needs, and PSU only covers frost temperatures, so neither page changes any field.
